title: Looking for 2–4 testers for a strategy-backtesting tool (free, no catch, honest feedback wanted)
author: DeliciousEquipment13
selftext:
Hi all — I've built a tool called Atlas Edge and I'm looking for 2–4 UK-based people to test it before any public launch.



What it actually is: a backtesting and automation platform. You connect your own IG account, build your own intraday strategy from a library of components (breakouts, trailing stops, filters, etc.), and the platform runs it through a genuinely rigorous statistical validation process — walk-forward testing, placebo controls, realistic cost modelling — before telling you honestly whether it holds up.



What it isn't: a signal service, an "AI trading bot," or anything promising guaranteed returns. It doesn't tell you what to trade. Most strategies people build (including my own, extensively) get correctly rejected — that's the tool working as intended, not a sales pitch gone wrong.



Why I'm posting this: I want people who aren't me actually using it, breaking it, and telling me honestly where it's confusing or annoying, before I open it up more broadly.



What's in it for you:



Free access during this test phase



Direct input into what gets built next



A genuinely rigorous way to test your own trading ideas before risking real money on them



Requirements:  18+, active

If you're interested, comment or DM me and I'll send over the details.

comments.author: ozgqr
comments.body: The combination of walk-forward testing, placebo controls, and realistic cost modelling is a strong way to expose overfitting. One thing I would watch is whether users can inspect the individual failure reasons—especially which regime, cost assumption, or parameter instability caused a rejection. That kind of traceability is also where Marx could be useful for an agent evaluating its own trading experiments.

comments.author: kush_patil
comments.body:
This is actually the kind of tool I’d enjoy trying to break 😅

If you want useful testing, I wouldn’t start with complicated strategies though. I’d start with something intentionally boring where every trade can be reconciled manually.

Then compare:  
signal → execution bar → fill → costs → exit → final metric  
If that all matches, start feeding it nasty cases: same-bar TP/SL ambiguity, high turnover, wider costs, unstable parameters, look-ahead mistakes, etc.

I’d also test whether the validation layer can reject a strategy that looks amazing in-sample but falls apart under slightly different parameters or walk-forward windows.

For a backtesting platform, I’d personally trust “we correctly killed 20 bad strategies” more than one beautiful equity curve.
